name: link-message-throughput
title: Link-message throughput
summary: Sustained delivery of small messages over one established link.

cell_notes.text: Prns returns proofs sooner, but RNS’s benchmark sender polls receipts every 0.5 ms. Prompt Prns proofs arrive in small batches, causing many poll/sleep/refill cycles. Stock’s slower proofs coalesce into larger batches, amortizing that loop better.

description: One link saturated with windowed small single-packet sends for a fixed wall-time - the same data shape as single-packet-throughput carried by the other mechanism: a session key amortizes the per-message crypto that singles pay per packet, while ProveAll still proves every delivery. The contrast between the two firehoses is the measurement.
conformance: attempted == sent + locally_culled, sent == responder_delivered, payload bytes match exactly, and wire timeouts are zero. Final reference receipts that lose their proof only after traffic stops remain explicit as receipt_unproved; they count as delivered only when the responder independently confirms the exact message and byte totals.
